title: Sioux City Animal Adoption & Rescue official gives tips to protect your pets this winter - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Prieto-Rivero Maren Ewertz ,
2 hours ago
SIOUX CITY , Iowa ( KCAU ) — The start of winter is already bringing extreme cold to areas, and when it comes to our pets, this cold weather can be especially dangerous.
If you have outdoor pets, local humane shelter officials say having an insulated shelter with a heated mat is important. You can also use straw, which is better than them lying directly on the cold ground.
Another thing to keep in mind is that pet owners are reminded to try to keep their pets more hydrated than usual.
“Even though it is cold out and you don’t think they drink as much water, they do need water, and there are heated water bowls,” said Cindy Rarrat with the Sioux City Animal Adoption & Rescue Center. “Heated buckets and stuff like that, you can keep water fresh, keep it open, so that they have something to drink.”
Story continues below
And, when it comes to their overall health and wellness in the winter, officials are reminding you that there are a few more things to consider.
“Running a humidifier, keeping the air moist. You can put booties on your dogs if they go outside to protect their feet from the cold, or you can use wax on the bottom of their feet to protect their feet if they have to go outside,” Rarrat said. “Usually limit their outdoor time because it’s so frigid to a maximum of 15 minutes. Let them go outside, do their business, and then bring them right back in.”
Pet owners are being reminded that when using salt to melt snow and ice, it is best to use a pet-friendly one, as the animals’ paws are sensitive.
